newsitem.title: SPAIN: Erdenet to expand Mongolia copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Erdenet to expand Mongolia copper mine.

text.p: Erdenet Mining Corporation, a Russian-Mongolian joint venture, plans to expand its mine and solvent-extraction (SX-EW) plant at Erdenet, Galsandorj Damba, Erdenet's U.K. representative said.
The mine, which commenced operations in 1978, is currently operating at full capacity, producing 21.5 million tonnes of ore a year.

"Although expansion plans to increase mine production to 30 million tonnes of ore by 2005 have been approved by the Mongolian Government," Damba said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.
The concentrates are railed via Russia and China to Europe and Asia, while some material is toll-smelted in Russia and then sold by Erdenet as cathode.
Although there is no smelting capacity at the primary mine, a small SX-EW plant started processing waste dumps and hills in February this year, Damba said.

Some 700 tonnes of low-cost copper has been produced, of which 420 tonnes has already been sold. The SX-EW plant is likely to be expanded in late-1999, with an eventual annual production target of 15,000 tonnes of refined copper, he said.
